landing_meta_description: {name} is a free, open-source surf forecast app. Live swell, wind and tide, and the forecast for 7 days, on one map. Save your spots, be told when they work, and log every session.
landing_hero_title: The surf forecast that {word} you when your spot works.
landing_hero_push_1_text: From 7 to 10: 1.8 m at 11 s from the west, wind 6 kn offshore, tide rising.
landing_hero_push_2_text: Until 12: 2.1 m at 12 s from the west-northwest, wind 8 kn offshore.
landing_hero_push_3_text: From 8 to 11: 1.5 m at 10 s from the southwest, tide falling.
landing_hero_push_4_text: From 17 to 20: 1.6 m at 13 s from the west, wind 4 kn offshore.
landing_hero_body: Live swell, wind and tide, and 7 days ahead, on one map.
landing_hero_free: Free · Open source · The map needs no account
landing_shot_alt: The {name} front page over its map of western Europe: the sea colored by its wave height, and the buoys with their latest reading.
landing_alert_more: Say what your spot needs, and {name} tells you when it works.
landing_alert_note: No more checking the forecast every morning. {name} does it for you.
landing_alert_way_text: By mail, by push, or both.
landing_features_title: Everything to surf at the right {moment}.
landing_features_more: The map needs no account. An account keeps your spots, alerts and sessions.
landing_sea_text: The whole coast in color, with arrows where the waves go, now and for the days ahead.
landing_buoys_text: What the sea is really doing, next to what was forecast.
landing_forecasts_text: Swell, wind and weather, anywhere on the coast.
landing_tides_text: High, low and the curve of the day.
landing_wind_text: Measured on the coast, and told as it meets your spot.
landing_spots_text: Private by default, shared with one link.
landing_sessions_text: Rate a session: {name} keeps what the sea did and learns what you like.
landing_community_text: Every line confirmed by those who surf it.
landing_open_text: No subscription, and open source. Improve the app, or ask for an API key and build your own version.
landing_sources_title: {live} buoys and wind, from the source.
landing_sources_more: {name} reads the public networks of buoys and wind stations, and open models. Each one is credited, with its licence.
sources_page_more: Who measured the sea {name} shows, how often it is read, and on what terms.
sources_named_text: Every figure says its source and its licence, in the app and in the API.
sources_open_text: Only sources whose terms allow it, read where they publish.
sources_kept_text: No data is taken from another app or another site.
sources_candhis_text: The national network of wave buoys along the French coasts, kept by Cerema with its partners.
sources_copernicus_in_situ_text: The buoys of the national institutes, Spain's and Ireland's among them, gathered by the European marine service.
sources_ndbc_text: The American network of buoys and coastal stations, which also relays its partners' around the world. Waves and wind.
sources_irish_lights_text: The buoys and weather stations of the Irish lighthouse service. Waves and wind.
sources_marine_institute_text: The weather buoys far off the Irish coast, M2 to M6. Waves and wind.
sources_hidrografico_text: The wave buoys of the Portuguese Navy's hydrographic institute.
sources_fmi_text: The wave buoys of the Finnish Meteorological Institute.
sources_queensland_text: The wave buoys of the Queensland Government, along its coast.
sources_meteo_france_text: The ground stations of the French weather service: wind and gusts.
sources_openwindmap_text: A community network of wind beacons, Pioupiou among them, often set right on the spots.
sources_dmi_text: The stations of the Danish weather service, many on lighthouses and harbours: wind and gusts.
sources_rijkswaterstaat_text: The stations of the Dutch authority of the coast: on the shore, on the Wadden and on the platforms of the North Sea.
sources_jma_text: AMeDAS, the automatic stations of the Japanese weather service, many on capes and harbours.
sources_coops_text: The weather sensors of NOAA's tide stations, on piers and harbours, on the shore itself: wind and gusts.
sources_ipma_text: The stations of the Portuguese weather institute, every hour.
sources_aemet_text: The automatic stations of the Spanish weather agency, with gusts, on an instance that holds a key.
sources_metar_text: The reports of the world's airports, where no other station stands near: wind and gusts.
sources_open_meteo_text: Wind and weather at any point from the models of DWD, Météo-France and NOAA, at 2 to 13 km, and the waves and the swell apart from Météo-France's model, at 8 km: read from the open files behind Open-Meteo's API, which answers itself when a file cannot be read.
sources_copernicus_models_text: The Met Office's fine model, at 1.5 km from the Vendée to Norway, and the map of wave heights.
sources_neaps_text: Tides computed from open harmonic constants, at the nearest port. They are not SHOM's predictions, so there is no coefficient yet.
sources_catalogue_text: The breaks the instance's operator added, completed by what accounts write of them. A spot an account makes public joins it under the ODbL.
sources_openfreemap_text: The map under everything, drawn from OpenStreetMap.
sources_natural_earth_text: The coastline that tells a wind station of the coast from one inland, so that a wide view shows the sea's wind first.
sources_photon_text: Finding a place by its name, for an account.
sources_missing_text: Tell me which one, and where it publishes. The technical detail of every source, its access and its terms, is in the repository.
landing_agents_more: They tell you if your spot works tomorrow: they read the sea, your spots and your sessions, and change nothing.
landing_agents_dev_text: An API and an MCP server, read-only, with a key. For now I hand the keys out myself: tell me what you're building.
landing_agents_chatgpt_steps: Turn on developer mode, create an app with this address, then sign in with your {name} account. Needs a paid plan.
landing_agents_claude_steps: Add a custom connector with this address, then sign in with your {name} account. Works without a subscription.
landing_agents_mcp_text: Read-only tools over Streamable HTTP, with one key and the limits of the API.
landing_agents_llms_text: What {name} is and how to call it, in plain text.
landing_agents_spec_text: Every route and its types, for a program.
landing_agents_docs_text: The same routes, for a person.
landing_agents_prompt: Read {url}, then use the {name} API to tell me what the sea does at my spot over the next three days: swell, wind and tide.
agents_tool_get_my_sessions_recap: What your log comes to: totals and the places surfed most
agents_tool_get_my_session: One session, with the conditions of that day
agents_tool_list_my_alerts: Your alerts, and the conditions each one waits for
agents_tool_get_surf_break_guide: The guide written by those who surf it: access, entry, hazards, rules
agents_tool_search_surf_breaks: A break by its name or its town's
agents_tool_list_surf_breaks: The breaks in an area, with what is known of each
agents_tool_get_tide_timeline: The tide's height, step by step
agents_tool_get_tide_extremes: High and low tides near a point
agents_tool_get_forecast: The hourly forecast of waves, wind and weather, up to 7 days
agents_tool_get_station_readings: What a station measured over a period
agents_tool_get_station: One station and its latest reading
agents_tool_list_stations: Buoys and wind stations in an area, with their latest reading
agents_tools_more: Every tool reads, none writes. Every answer says where its data comes from, and under which licence.
agents_account_more: In Claude or ChatGPT, with no key: the assistant asks you to sign in to {name}, then reads the sea and what your account keeps. It changes nothing.
agents_page_more: An MCP server and an API, read-only: buoys, wind, forecasts, tides and breaks, each with its source.
agents_meta_description: Plug Claude, ChatGPT or your own code into {name}: buoys, wind, forecasts, tides and breaks, read-only, each with its source.
landing_story_me: I finally brought surfing and code together.
landing_story_origin_after: , made by Thomas. It made me want to build my own, with what I was missing: spots, the conditions that make them work, alerts, and much more. Thanks to him.
landing_story_feedback: I'm building it alone, and the app is young. If something's off, write to me: every message counts.
landing_next_more: Nothing here is promised: tell me which one you're waiting for most.
landing_next_mobile_text: iOS and Android, with alerts as notifications.
landing_next_data_text: New measuring networks, and a much fuller catalogue of spots.
landing_next_tides_text: And times matched to the official tables, where their licence allows.
landing_next_yours_text: Tell me what you're missing, it comes straight to my inbox.
landing_idea_text: A feature, an improvement, a buoy that's missing. It reaches me by mail, and I answer at your address.
landing_idea_placeholder: What would you like {name} to do?
landing_idea_sent_text: Your idea reached me. I'll answer at the address you gave.

terms_public_title: What you ask to make public
terms_public_text: You may ask that a spot be made public. A moderator checks that it is known to all, and may refuse. If it is accepted, its name, its point and its guide join the catalogue of {name} under the Open Database License (ODbL) 1.0: anyone may reuse them, provided they name the source and share what they make of them under the same terms. Your account is not named there.
terms_public_rights: By sending the request, you confirm that you may publish this information, and you agree to that licence. A spot that was made public stays public when your account is deleted.

analytics_description: The app is just getting started. With your permission, it tells me which features you use and sends me a report when something breaks, so I can see what works and fix what doesn’t. Your spots, searches and what you write are never sent.
analytics_errors_description: Send a report when something breaks. It never holds your spots, searches or what you write.
analytics_terms: With your permission, the app sends PostHog an opaque account or device ID, technical session identifiers, the features you use, and a report of each error it did not handle: its kind, its message with addresses, emails and identifiers removed, and where in the code it happened. Your spot locations, searches and written content are excluded. Refusing does not limit the app. Change your choice in the account settings, where you can also turn off the error reports alone.
legal_meta_description: Who publishes {name}, who hosts it, and under which licence its code is open.
legal_publisher_text: {name} is published by {publisher}, a private individual, on a non-professional basis. {publisher} is also its director of publication.
legal_code_text: The code of {name} is open source, under the GNU AGPL, version 3: whoever runs another instance of it is that instance's publisher. The measurements and forecasts belong to the networks and models that publish them, each under its own terms.
privacy_meta_description: What {name} keeps of its visitors and its accounts, why, for how long, and who receives it.
privacy_who_text: This page says what {name} keeps about you, why, who else receives it, and how to have it corrected or deleted. {publisher} runs this instance and is responsible for this data. Write to this address about any of it:
privacy_visit_text: Reading the map takes no account. Cloudflare serves the web app, so it receives your IP address and the pages you open, as any host does. To draw the map, your browser loads its tiles from OpenFreeMap and the colours of the sea from Copernicus Marine: both see your IP address and the part of the map you look at.
privacy_visit_browser: Your browser keeps your settings for the app: your language in a cookie, and in its own storage the map's last position, its layers, your units, your shortcuts and the places you looked at last. Without an account they stay there, and none of them tracks you.
privacy_visit_audience: Umami, which {publisher} runs, counts the pages read here, the landing's too: the page, the site you came from, your browser, your system, the kind and size of your screen, your language and your country. It sets no cookie and keeps neither your IP address nor the page's query, and it tells two visits of one browser apart by a code that changes every month.
privacy_account_text: An account keeps your email address, your username, which others can read, and your password, stored hashed and never in clear. A cookie keeps your session open. At sign-up, a mail with a link checks your address, and the link works for a day. If you forget your password, a mail with a link lets you choose another: the link works once, for an hour, and choosing signs your account out everywhere. If you sign in with Google, Google gives us your name, your email address and your profile picture, and the tokens of that sign-in are kept with your account. Google tells us nothing else.
privacy_account_sessions: Each sign-in is kept with the IP address and the browser it came from, for the security of your account. Nothing in the app shows them, and they are kept as long as the account exists.
privacy_content_text: The app keeps what you make in it: your spots and lists, your alerts and what they told you, your log of sessions with its notes and what the sea did, the places you looked at last, your units and your shortcuts. Your spots and sessions are yours alone. Others read something of yours only in these cases:
privacy_content_shared: A list you share by a link is read by whoever has the link, with the private spots in it.
privacy_content_public: A spot you ask to make public is read by the operator who decides. Once accepted, it joins the catalogue without your name.
privacy_content_guides: What you write in a guide is read by everyone, under your username, once it is confirmed.
privacy_content_friends: Your friends read your username, your rank and your confirmed contributions.
privacy_content_operator: The operator of the instance reads each account's email address and username, whether the address is checked and whether the account is suspended. {publisher} runs the server and can read the database, but reads it only to keep the service running or to answer a request.
privacy_alerts_mail: Unosend sends the mail that checks your address, the one that lets you choose a new password and, if you choose alerts by mail, the mails of your alerts. It receives your address, the names of the alert and of its spots, and what the alert found. You may leave the names out of the subject. Each alert mail has a link that stops them, and no mail carries a tracker.
privacy_alerts_push: If you turn on push in a browser, we keep the address its push service gave it, its keys and the name of the browser. Each push goes through that service, run by Google, Mozilla, Apple or Microsoft depending on your browser, encrypted so that the service cannot read it. A browser is forgotten when you sign out of it or remove it.
privacy_search_text: When you search for a place by its name, our server asks Photon, a service of komoot, in Germany. It sends what you typed, your language and the centre of the map, rounded to about ten kilometres, and nothing about your account. The search is neither kept nor logged.
privacy_agents_text: If you sign an AI assistant in to your account, we keep its registration, your agreement and its tokens. It can then read your spots, your alerts, what they told you and your sessions, and change nothing. Its access lasts an hour and renews itself for up to 30 days after it was last used. You disconnect it from your account's panel. What the assistant does with what it read is up to whoever provides it.
privacy_analytics_more: PostHog keeps these events and reports in its European cloud. They reach it through the app's own address, without your IP address, and PostHog is told not to locate you. Your choice is kept in your browser for six months, then asked again. The landing page sends PostHog nothing.
privacy_contact_text: The forms of this site that write to {publisher} send your first name, your address and your message by mail to {email}. Nothing of them is kept in the database: the mail is all there is.
privacy_running_text: The API counts its calls by hour, by kind of caller and by outcome, never by account. What you ask of the forecasts is counted apart, by the hour, to your account, or to a hash of your IP address when you have none, so that one caller cannot spend the day's forecasts of everyone: these counts are kept two days. Its log notes each request's method, path and status, without your IP address. What an operator does, such as suspending an account, is recorded with that account's identifier. The database is backed up by its host. When the API itself fails, it sends PostHog a report of the fault: what failed and where in its code, with nothing of the request, the account or the person who made it.
privacy_bases_contract: Your account, what you save, mails and push, place search and assistants: providing the service you asked for (GDPR, article 6(1)(b)).
privacy_bases_consent: Usage analytics and the app's error reports: your consent (article 6(1)(a)), which you withdraw at any time in the account's panel.
privacy_bases_interest: Audience counts, sign-in records, call counts, the log, the API's fault reports, backups and moderation: our legitimate interest in keeping the service secure and running (article 6(1)(f)).
privacy_bases_messages: Messages you send us: our legitimate interest in answering them (article 6(1)(f)).
privacy_does_api: hosts the server of the API and its database
privacy_does_analytics: usage analytics and error reports, if you agree to them, and the API's fault reports
privacy_does_tiles: the map's tiles, which your browser loads
privacy_does_sea: the maps of the sea, which your browser loads
privacy_recipients_transfer: Cloudflare, Google and Unosend are in the United States. Cloudflare and Google take part in the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, under which the European Commission holds that data sent to them is adequately protected. Unosend receives it under the standard contractual clauses of the European Commission, which its data processing agreement includes.
privacy_recipients_none: Nobody else receives your data. It is never sold, and the app shows no advertising.
privacy_keep_account: Your account and what you save in it: until the account is deleted.
privacy_keep_counts: Call counts and the record of what operators did: 13 months.
privacy_keep_mails: The count of mails sent to an account, which limits them: 2 days.
privacy_keep_consent: Your choice about analytics and error reports: 6 months, in your browser.
privacy_keep_backups: The database's backups keep a copy until newer backups replace them.
privacy_keep_after: A spot that was made public, and what you wrote in guides, stay after your account is deleted, naming nobody.
privacy_rights_text: You may ask for a copy of what we keep about you, in a format a program can read, and ask that it be corrected or deleted, that its use be limited, or object to it. Write to {email} from your account's address: you get an answer within a month.
privacy_rights_delete: The app has no button to delete an account yet. Ask {email}, and your account is deleted, with everything it holds, within a month.
privacy_rights_cnil: If you think your data is mishandled, you may complain to the CNIL, the French data protection authority:
privacy_changes_text: When this page changes, the date at its top changes too.
terms_about_text: {name} shows surf conditions: buoy measurements, forecasts, tides and a catalogue of surf breaks. It lets you save spots and be alerted when the sea matches. It is free, and published by {publisher}. These terms apply to anyone who uses it, and creating an account means you accept them. The privacy policy says what is kept about you.
terms_figures_text: Measurements, forecasts and tides come from other networks and models. They can be wrong, late or missing, and an alert can arrive late or not at all. Look at the sea yourself before you go in. {name} decides nothing for you, and {publisher} is not liable for what you decide from it, within the limits the law allows.
terms_figures_sources: Each source keeps its own terms:
terms_account_text: An account is one person's. Give an address that is yours, and keep your password to yourself. Your username is read by others: choose one that passes for no one else and offends no one. An operator may take a username away, and you then choose another.
terms_use_text: Do not use {name} to break the law, to harass anyone, or to write what you know is false about a place. Do not try to read what is not yours, to get round a limit, or to load the service so that others cannot use it. A program reads the API with a key, within that key's limits.
terms_use_suspension: An operator may suspend an account that breaks these terms: it can no longer sign in. Write to {email} if you think that was a mistake.
terms_service_title: A free service, as it is
terms_service_text: {name} is free and shows no advertising. It comes as it is: it may stop working for a while, change or close, and an operator may close the map to visitors without an account.
terms_service_leave: You may stop using it at any time, and have your account deleted: the privacy policy says how.
terms_changes_text: When these terms change, the date at the top of this page changes too. Using {name} after a change means you accept the new terms.
terms_changes_law: These terms are governed by French law. If something goes wrong, write to {email} first.
